_note: Daily pop-up on rcflithelp.com: one highlight per day, the same for every visitor (Sri Lanka date), shown once a day. Items rotate in this order and start again at the top. Fields: kind (the small label), title, text (one or two short sentences), link (a page on this site), cta (button text), img (optional: a text's slug, to show its thumbnail). Add, remove or reorder freely; build.js checks that every link exists.

items.title: RCF Practice Paper 1
items.text: A full O/L 2026 paper in the latest format, with model answers and a PDF to print. Try it under exam conditions: one hour for Paper I, two for Paper II.

items.title: To the Nile by John Keats
items.text: A sonnet that moves from wonder at the river's legends to a calm, realistic picture. Read the line-by-line analysis and the Sinhala translation.

items.title: Context questions: 5 marks each
items.text: In Paper I, Section A, part (a) is 1 mark for naming the text AND the author. Learn every author's full name: it is the easiest mark in the paper.

items.title: A 15-minute sonnet
items.text: Keats wrote 'To the Nile' in 1818 in a friendly contest with Shelley and Leigh Hunt: each poet had fifteen minutes to write a sonnet on the Nile.

items.title: The Eagle by Tennyson
items.text: Only six lines, but a favourite in exams. The guide covers the poem line by line, with a Sinhala translation, techniques and model essays.

items.title: The Lumber Room by Saki
items.text: A clever boy, a strict aunt and a locked room full of wonders. How does Saki use humour and irony to take the child's side?

items.title: How essays are marked
items.text: Each Paper II essay is worth 15 marks: Content 7, Organisation 4 and Language 4. Plan an introduction, three or four clear points with quotations, and a conclusion.

items.title: The first Latin American Nobel
items.text: Gabriela Mistral, the poet of 'Fear', was the first Latin American writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1945.

items.title: RCF Practice Paper 2
items.text: Fear and courage; love, loyalty and pride. Paper I extracts, Section B novel questions and 14 essay questions, all with answers.

items.title: War is Kind by Stephen Crane
items.text: The title says the opposite of what the poet means. See how irony, refrain and harsh images expose the cruelty of war.

items.title: Section B: choose one novel
items.text: In Paper I, Section B, answer only ONE of the three novel extracts. The marks are 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 4, and the 4-mark question wants a theme explained, not just named.

items.title: Bringing Tony Home
items.text: A boy, his dog and the pain of parting. The guide covers the author, setting, plot, characters, themes and exam-style questions.

items.title: A doctor who wrote plays
items.text: Anton Chekhov, who wrote 'The Bear', was a medical doctor. He once called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress.

items.title: Twilight of a Crane
items.text: Love, sacrifice and greed in a modern play built on a Japanese folk tale. Who is really to blame for Tsu's departure?

items.title: RCF Practice Paper 3
items.text: Freedom and imprisonment; justice and mercy. Download the question paper with ruled answer lines and mark it with the answer guide.

items.title: Once Upon a Time by Gabriel Okara
items.text: A father tells his son how people have learnt to 'wear many faces'. A study guide with a stanza-by-stanza analysis and exam questions.

items.title: Quote, then explain
items.text: Examiners reward short, accurate quotations that support your point. Write the quotation, then explain what it shows: never let a quotation stand on its own.

items.title: Mark Twain's real name
items.text: Mark Twain, author of 'The Prince and the Pauper', was really Samuel Clemens. 'Mark twain' was a river-boat call meaning two fathoms of safe water.

items.title: Test yourself on A Bird Came Down the Walk
items.text: Read the analysis of Emily Dickinson's poem, watch the video, then try the quiz at the end of the page.

items.title: The Lahore Attack
items.text: Kumar Sangakkara's account of the 2009 attack on the Sri Lankan team: calm, courage, humility and pride. A guide with exam questions.

items.title: RCF Practice Paper 4
items.text: Crime, loyalty and conscience; appearance and reality. A complete paper with answers and an essay marking guide.

items.title: Emily Dickinson's hidden poems
items.text: Emily Dickinson wrote about 1,800 poems, but very few were published in her lifetime. Most were found by her sister after her death.

items.title: Two's Company by Raymond Wilson
items.text: A man who laughs at ghosts spends a night in a haunted house. Watch how the brackets reveal his fear, right up to the twist ending.

items.title: Use the reading time
items.text: You get 10 minutes of extra reading time. Use it to choose your Section B novel and your four Paper II essays before you start writing.

items.title: The Nightingale and the Rose
items.text: A bird gives her life for a student's love, and he throws the rose away. What is Oscar Wilde saying about love and logic?

items.title: Kipling's Nobel Prize
items.text: Rudyard Kipling, who wrote 'The Camel's Hump', won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1907, the first English-language writer to receive it.

items.title: RCF Practice Paper 5
items.text: Power and humility; endings and new beginnings. Finish the set and you will have answered questions on every set text.

items.title: The Vendor of Sweets
items.text: Jagan, Mali and Grace in Malgudi: father and son, tradition and modernity. The guide includes context and essay questions.

items.title: Richard Cory by E.A. Robinson
items.text: Rich, admired and 'everything' the town wished to be, until the shocking last line. A poem about appearance and reality.

items.title: Three Nobel Prize winners
items.text: Three writers on your syllabus won the Nobel Prize in Literature: Rudyard Kipling in 1907, Gabriela Mistral in 1945 and Wislawa Szymborska ('The Terrorist, He's Watching') in 1996.

items.title: Answer the question asked
items.text: Essay questions often begin with a statement: 'Do you agree?' Say clearly whether you agree, then prove it with examples. Do not just retell the story.

items.title: Fear by Gabriela Mistral
items.text: A mother does not want her little girl turned into a swallow, a princess or a queen. Is her love beautiful, possessive, or both?

items.title: The Bear by Anton Chekhov
items.text: A widow in mourning, a furious creditor, a duel with pistols, and a proposal. See how Chekhov turns a quarrel into a farce.

items.title: A Sri Lankan film-maker
items.text: Tissa Abeysekara, author of 'Bringing Tony Home', was a well-known Sri Lankan film director and screenwriter, which is why his novel feels so visual.

items.title: The Huntsman by Edward Lowbury
items.text: 'Talking brought me here.' A folk tale in verse with a chilling twist. The study guide explains the irony and the moral.

items.title: Saki's real name
items.text: 'Saki', author of 'The Lumber Room', was the pen name of Hector Hugh Munro. As a boy he was brought up by strict aunts, much like Nicholas.

items.title: The full syllabus on one page
items.text: Every prescribed poem, prose text, play and novel, grouped by theme, with links to the notes. A good place to plan your revision.

items.title: Past papers and marking schemes
items.text: Official O/L papers, term tests and model papers to download, together with the RCF Practice Papers for 2026.
